# `lcmv`

the LCMV beamformer of a head model, a data covariance and a noise covariance (Brainstorm 2016 or MNE-Python make_lcmv conventions).

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run lcmv --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run lcmv --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --block-seconds <10000 samples> --divisor samples_minus_one --name rest_data_cov
nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording emptyroom --all --block-seconds <10000 samples> --divisor samples_minus_one --name emptyroom_noise_cov
nxr-neuro run lcmv --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --data-cov rest_data_cov --noise-cov emptyroom_noise_cov [--forward NAME]
nxr-neuro run bandpass --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --lower 7 --upper 13 --name rest_alpha
nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest_alpha --all --name rest_alpha_cov
nxr-neuro run lcmv --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --conventions mne --data-cov rest_alpha_cov --noise-cov emptyroom_noise_cov --pick-ori max-power --name LCMV_alpha
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `forward` | operator forward, where {"name": "$forward"} | yes |
| `data_covariance` | statistic any, where {"measure": "covariance", "name": "$data_cov"} | yes |
| `noise_covariance` | statistic any, where {"measure": "covariance", "name": "$noise_cov"}, required false (the empty room's covariance: `nxr-neuro run noisecov` on it (required under conventions brainstorm)) | no |
| `sources` | manifold surface, is forward.from | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `forward` | `--forward` | `none` | - |  | the head model's name, or none: the subject's one head model |
| `data_cov` | `--data-cov` | `required` | - |  | the data covariance's name: a statistic of the recording the kernel is for (`nxr-neuro run noisecov` on it) |
| `noise_cov` | `--noise-cov` | none | - |  | the noise covariance's name: a statistic of the empty room (`nxr-neuro run noisecov` on it), covering the data covariance's channels; required under brainstorm; null (mne only): an identity covariance |
| `conventions` | `--conventions` | `brainstorm` | - | brainstorm, mne | brainstorm (Brainstorm 2016: fixed orientation, the pseudo neural activity index) \| mne (MNE-Python's make_lcmv) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{forward}_lcmv` | - |  | the kernel's name; beside it <name>_channels, <name>_whitener and <name>_data_whitener |
| `regularisation` | `--regularisation` | `median` | - | median, ridge, diagonal, none | brainstorm: how each covariance is regularised after truncation to its rank, type by type: median (the eigenvalue tail set to the median: the reference's) \| ridge \| diagonal \| none |
| `ridge_fraction` | `--ridge-fraction` | `0.1` | fraction |  | brainstorm: the ridge's fraction of the largest eigenvalue (ridge only; the reference passes 0.1 with median, where it has no effect) |
| `detect_diagonal` | `--detect-diagonal` | true | - |  | brainstorm: a diagonal noise covariance whitens both covariances by their diagonal (the reference's rule) |
| `reg` | `--reg` | none | fraction |  | mne: the diagonal loading of the whitened data covariance, a fraction of its mean singular value (MNE-Python's reg); null: 0.05 |
| `pick_ori` | `--pick-ori` | none | - | None, free, normal, max-power | mne: free (three rows a source, x y z) \| normal (along the source surface's normals) \| max-power (each source's orientation of most power, its sign along the normal); null: free |
| `weight_norm` | `--weight-norm` | none | - | None, none, unit-noise-gain, unit-noise-gain-invariant, nai | mne: none (unit gain, A.m) \| unit-noise-gain \| unit-noise-gain-invariant \| nai (the neural activity index); null: unit-noise-gain-invariant (MNE-Python's default) |
| `rank` | `--rank` | none | - |  | mne: the covariances' rank, info (per modality: its channels less the projectors on them) or an integer (one modality only, e.g. the rank after Maxwell filtering); null: info |
| `average_reference` | `--average-reference` | true | - |  | apply the average reference of EEG, sEEG and ECoG (brainstorm: to the gain and both covariances, per family; mne: as a projector, as MNE-Python requires) |
| `normals` | `--normals` | `brainstorm` | - | brainstorm, corner_angle | the sources' orientations: brainstorm (the reference's VertNormals: minus the sum of the incident faces' unit normals, normalised) \| corner_angle (geometry-central's corner-angle weighted normals) |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.lcmv`](../nodes.md) | forward=forward, data_covariance=data_covariance, noise_covariance=noise_covariance, sources=sources | conventions=$conventions, regularisation=$regularisation, ridge_fraction=$ridge_fraction, detect_diagonal=$detect_diagonal, reg=$reg, pick_ori=$pick_ori, weight_norm=$weight_norm, rank=$rank, average_reference=$average_reference, normals=$normals | kernel, channels, whitener, data_whitener |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `kernel` | kind operator, operator_kind inverse kernel, name $name, from forward.to, to forward.from, from_selection channels, derived_from forward |
| `channels` | kind selection, type indices, name $name_channels, on forward.to |
| `whitener` | kind operator, operator_kind whitener, name $name_whitener, from forward.to, to forward.to, from_selection channels, to_selection channels, of_statistic noise_covariance |
| `data_whitener` | kind operator, operator_kind whitener, name $name_data_whitener, from forward.to, to forward.to, from_selection channels, to_selection channels, of_statistic data_covariance |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE LCMV BEAMFORMER of a subject, from a head model (an operator of kind forward, gain channels x 3 sources), a DATA covariance and a NOISE covariance (statistics over one pick of the
head model's channels, both made by `nxr-neuro run noisecov`: the data covariance on the recording the kernel is for, or on its band-passed copy (`run bandpass`, then `run noisecov` on
its output), the noise covariance on the empty room) and the source surface, whose vertex normals orient the sources. Two conventions (`--conventions`):

brainstorm (the default): fixed orientation, the pseudo neural activity index. Written from Van Veen et al. 1997 and the documented behaviour of Brainstorm's 2016 source estimation
(process_inverse_2016 / bst_inverse_linear_2016, LCMV, measure NAI, orientation fixed, regularisation median) of its release of 2018-10-12, the version the MEG fingerprinting paper used
(da Silva Castanheira J, Orozco Perez HD, Misic B, Baillet S (2021) Nat Commun 12:5713, doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25895-8; megFingerprinting v1.0.0, 06fdba8). Each covariance is truncated
to its rank and regularised type by type; the kernel row of a source is (W_d l)^T W_d / ||W_d l|| (W_d the data whitener, l the gain along the normal). Stored: the kernel `<name>` (scalar),
its channels `<name>_channels`, the noise whitener `<name>_whitener` (the reference stores it; the kernel does not use it) and the data whitener `<name>_data_whitener`.

mne: MNE-Python's make_lcmv (1.13.2) with its defaults (reg 0.05, rank 'info', no depth weighting, pick_ori None, weight_norm 'unit-noise-gain-invariant') and its options pick_ori
(free | normal | max-power) and weight_norm (none | unit-noise-gain | unit-noise-gain-invariant | nai). The noise covariance is optional (none: an identity covariance, one sensor type
only) and whitens the gain and the data covariance; the projectors of the data's recording (with the average reference) are in its whitener. Stored: the kernel `<name>` (sources x
channels; 3 rows a source, x y z, for free orientation), its channels and the noise whitener `<name>_whitener` the kernel ends with (none without a noise covariance).

Every stored result carries its references (producer_json.references).
It cannot resolve: correlated sources (they partly cancel); a weight-normalised output is an index relative to the data covariance's span, not a current; the regularisation trades
resolution for stability.

  nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --block-seconds <10000 samples> --divisor samples_minus_one --name rest_data_cov
  nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording emptyroom --all --block-seconds <10000 samples> --divisor samples_minus_one --name emptyroom_noise_cov
  nxr-neuro run lcmv --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --data-cov rest_data_cov --noise-cov emptyroom_noise_cov [--forward NAME]
  nxr-neuro run bandpass --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --lower 7 --upper 13 --name rest_alpha
  nxr-neuro run noisecov --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest_alpha --all --name rest_alpha_cov
  nxr-neuro run lcmv --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --conventions mne --data-cov rest_alpha_cov --noise-cov emptyroom_noise_cov --pick-ori max-power --name LCMV_alpha
```
